meta.expect: 'put it in an email', no list

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have until then. Owen found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of a class, nobody called me first, and I want to know who decided that and on what basis.
I didn't come for the thanks. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in, yes or no?
Let me show you the version history. The document was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, and 1,406 words arrived in two pastes six minutes apart.

Turn that screen toward me, I'll read it myself. Owen wrote that essay over the weekend, and a paste tells you where the text landed, not who wrote it. You still haven't told me whether anyone heard him before the zero went in.
Can you summarize what we've agreed so far in bullet points?
Put it in an email yourself, and it'll be short, because nothing's been agreed. The zero comes off, I get an apology, and nothing about this touches Owen's record.
Just a quick numbered list is fine.
No lists, Hale. You'll have my position in writing tonight, and right now it's one line: the zero comes off. Now answer my question about Owen.
